title: TATAR unified triage summary
description: Shared summary.json contract emitted by every TATAR collector (Windows Tatar.ps1, Linux tatar-linux.sh, and future macOS/Android editions). One parser / dashboard ingests all platforms.

tool.description: Human tool name, e.g. 'TATAR Triage Toolkit'.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS shared schema. Consumers key off this.

privileged.description: Ran with elevated rights (Administrator on Windows, root on Unix).

durationSeconds.description: Wall-clock collection duration in seconds (unified across platforms).

environment.description: Execution context of the collected host. All fields best-effort; 'unknown'/'none' when undetermined.

virtualization.description: e.g. kvm, vmware, hyperv, xen, none, unknown.

securityModule.description: Linux: selinux-enforcing/permissive, apparmor, none. Windows: defender or none.

modulesSkipped.description: Modules that were requested but never ran (unknown module name). Empty on a clean run. A non-empty list means evidence is MISSING, not absent.

stats.description: Key/value counters. A counter is emitted as a JSON number on every platform. Use the canonical key in x-canonicalStatKeys for a concept any collector can measure, so one dashboard can plot 'accounts on host' without a per-platform special case; a key listed there means the same thing everywhere. Platform-specific counters are allowed, but a new spelling of an existing concept is not.

findingsCount.description: Length of findings[]; equals activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount.

activeFindingsCount.description: Findings still on the headline list. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length. A low value means 'allowlisted' only when suppressedCount is high - it never means the host is clean.

suppressedCount.description: Findings hidden by an allowlist rule but retained in findings[] for audit. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length.

findings.description: Automated triage leads (NOT verdicts). Each maps to zero or more MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

severity.description: The shipped collectors emit only High and Review. Info is reserved for low-signal context findings; a consumer may receive it from a future collector, so handle it, but do not expect it today.

category.description: Emitting module/collector, e.g. process, users, persistence.

technique.description: Suggested MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs. Empty when unmapped.

detail.description: Where to look / why it matters.

confidence.description: How sure the tool is (independent of severity).

suppressed.description: True when hidden from the headline by an allowlist rule (still retained for audit).

suppressReason.description: Why the finding was suppressed (allowlist rule / signature).

iocMatch.description: True when an IOC matched this finding. The indicator itself is prefixed into detail as: IOC match: <indicator> | ...

then.description: The three counts are optional for schemaVersion 1.1, which predates them, and mandatory from 1.2 on - every 1.2 producer emits them and four test harnesses assert the invariant.
